# FlowForm - Complete Endpoint & AI Agent Documentation

<!-- source: docs/guide/ai-agents.md -->

# AI Coding Agents Quickstart

A deterministic guide for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, v0, Lovable, Bolt) adding a form or reading submissions from a FlowForm instance.

---

## Add a Contact Form in 3 Steps

### 1. Create an Endpoint Form

Create an **Endpoint** form (`type: "endpoint"`) in the FlowForm admin panel or programmatically via the `create_form` MCP tool.

- **Redirect handling:** Never pass a relative path (like `/thank-you`) in `_next` because relative paths resolve on the FlowForm host, not your app. Instead, set **Redirect URL** in the FlowForm form settings, or pass an absolute `_next` URL whose domain is listed in the form's **Allowed Domains** (or `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`).
- **Mail notifications (optional):** Self-hosted deployments use the instance's configured SMTP provider in Admin Panel -> Mail Settings.

### 2. Copy the Form Slug

Record the FlowForm base URL (for example `https://forms.example.com` or `http://localhost:8000`) and the form `slug` (for example `contact-us`). Both `POST /f/{slug}` and `POST /api/v1/f/{slug}` also accept the form `access_key` or `uuid`.

### 3. Paste the Form Snippet

Use a standard HTML form when the browser navigates on submit, or JSON `fetch` when submitting inline without a page reload. Include the hidden `_gotcha` honeypot input in every form.

#### Option A: Zero-JS HTML Form (`POST /f/{slug}`)

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />

  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send Message</button>
</form>
```

For Astro, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Hugo/Eleventy/Jekyll, or server/mobile clients, see the stack-specific guides:
- [Endpoints Overview](/guide/endpoints/)
- [HTML Forms](/guide/endpoints/html)
- [JavaScript (fetch & FormData)](/guide/endpoints/javascript)
- [Next.js](/guide/endpoints/nextjs)
- [Astro](/guide/endpoints/astro)
- [Nuxt](/guide/endpoints/nuxt)
- [SvelteKit](/guide/endpoints/sveltekit)
- [Static Site Generators](/guide/endpoints/static-site-generators)
- [Mobile & Server Clients](/guide/endpoints/mobile-and-servers)

#### Option B: Browser JavaScript (`POST /api/v1/f/{slug}`)

```html
<form id="contact-form">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />
  <input type="text" name="name" required placeholder="Your name" />
  <input type="email" name="email" required placeholder="you@example.com" />
  <textarea name="message" required placeholder="How can we help?"></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
  <p id="form-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
</form>

<script>
  const form = document.getElementById('contact-form');
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('form-status');

  form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const payload = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form).entries());

    const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });

    const result = await response.json();
    if (response.ok && result.success) {
      statusEl.textContent = 'Message sent.';
      form.reset();
    } else {
      statusEl.textContent = result.error || 'Submission failed.';
    }
  });
</script>
```

---

## Exact Response Contract

- `POST /f/{slug}` accepts `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data`, or JSON. When `Accept: application/json` is absent and the form has a **Redirect URL** (or a valid `_next` / `_redirect`), it responds with `302 Found`. Otherwise it returns `200 OK` JSON.
- `POST /api/v1/f/{slug}` always responds with JSON and never redirects.

### Success (`200 OK`)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Submission received",
  "id": "22c7a46f-fca5-4ad8-8348-14ccd6fd7cb0"
}
```

When `_gotcha` or `_honeypot` is non-empty, FlowForm discards the submission and returns `200 OK` with `"id": null`.

### Errors

| Status | Cause | Body |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `403` | `Origin` / `Referer` not in the form's Allowed Domains, or the form requires a server secret (`X-FlowForm-Secret` header / `?_secret=`) that is missing or wrong | `{"success": false, "error": "..."}` with `Submissions are not permitted from this domain origin.`, `Endpoint secret is required.` or `Invalid endpoint secret.` |
| `404` | Form slug not found, form is inactive, or form is not in `endpoint` mode | `{"success": false, "error": "Form endpoint not found or inactive."}` |
| `422` | Missing/invalid captcha token (`cf-turnstile-response` / `h-captcha-response`), or uploaded file violates size/MIME rules | `{"success": false, "error": "...", "errors": {...}}` |
| `429` | Per-IP rate limit (`10` req/min/IP), or the owner's quota is exhausted on instances that enable metering (`FLOWFORM_METERING_ENABLED`, off by default) | `{"success": false, "error": "..."}` or standard throttle JSON |

---

## Honeypot & Reserved Control Fields

FlowForm strips these reserved fields from saved submission data:

- `_gotcha`, `_honeypot`: Silent anti-spam trap. Keep hidden and empty for real users.
- `_next`, `_redirect`: Optional redirect target for `POST /f/{slug}`. Must be an absolute URL matching `APP_URL`, the form's **Allowed Domains**, or `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`.
- `_token`, `_method`, `_secret`, `_source`, `cf-turnstile-response`, `_turnstile`, `g-recaptcha-response`, `h-captcha-response`, `_hcaptcha`: also stripped automatically. `_source` (e.g. `?_source=astro`) is kept as attribution in the submission's metadata.
- `_replyto` is not stripped: it is stored like any other field and becomes the Reply-To of notification emails (falling back to `reply_to`, then `email`).
- File uploads (`<input type="file" name="attachment" />` with `enctype="multipart/form-data"`) are supported directly on endpoint forms.

---

## Connecting via MCP (`POST /api/v1/mcp`)

FlowForm exposes a JSON-RPC 2.0 Model Context Protocol endpoint at `POST /api/v1/mcp`. Authentication via a Laravel Sanctum bearer token is required. Create a scoped token in **Admin Panel -> API Tokens** or via Artisan (`php artisan token:create`).

### Required Token Abilities & Tools

| Tool Name | Required Ability | Arguments | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `list_forms` | `forms:read` | `limit` (integer, optional, default `20`, max `50`) | List active FlowForm endpoints and wizards visible to the user |
| `get_form_schema` | `forms:read` | `identifier` (string, required: UUID or slug) | Fetch steps, fields, options, captcha settings, and conditions |
| `create_form` | `forms:write` | `name` (string, required), `slug` (string), `type` (`"endpoint"` \| `"wizard"`), `is_encrypted` (boolean), `webhook_url` (string), `steps` (string[]) | Create a new endpoint or multi-step form |
| `submit_form` | `submissions:write` | `form_slug` (string, required), `data` (object, required) | Store a submission payload and dispatch webhooks |
| `list_submissions` | `submissions:read` | `form_slug` (string, required), `limit` (integer, optional, default `10`, max `30`) | List recent submissions for a form |

### Example MCP Calls

Initialize and list available tools:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'
```

Create an endpoint form via MCP:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 2,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "create_form",
      "arguments": {
        "name": "Contact Us",
        "slug": "contact-us",
        "type": "endpoint"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Inspect available forms via MCP:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 3,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "list_forms",
      "arguments": {"limit": 20}
    }
  }'
```

You can also inspect the full AI-readable reference bundle at [/llms.txt](/llms.txt) and [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt).

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/index.md -->

# Submit From Any Stack

FlowForm lets any website, app, or server send form submissions to a single hosted or self-hosted endpoint without building your own backend.

Create an **Endpoint** form in the FlowForm admin panel, copy its `slug` or `access_key`, and point your form or HTTP client to it.

---

## Endpoint URLs

Every active Endpoint form exposes two routes. Both accept your form's `slug`, `access_key`, or `uuid`:

| Route | Intended Caller | Default Success Response |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST https://forms.example.com/f/{slug}` | HTML `<form action="...">` | `302 Redirect` to `_next` / `redirect_url` (or `200 JSON` if none set) |
| `POST https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/{slug}` | JavaScript `fetch`, mobile apps, server-to-server | `200 JSON` (`{ "success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>" }`) |

If you send `Accept: application/json` to `/f/{slug}`, FlowForm also returns JSON instead of redirecting.

---

## Reserved Fields

FlowForm strips reserved control fields before saving submission data so they never clutter your inbox or database:

| Field | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `_gotcha`, `_honeypot` | Anti-spam honeypot. If either field is non-empty, FlowForm returns a normal success response without saving the submission or sending notifications. |
| `_next`, `_redirect` | Redirect target after an HTML `<form>` submission. Use an absolute URL whose host matches the FlowForm instance's `APP_URL` or is listed in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`. A relative path such as `/thank-you` redirects to that path **on the FlowForm host**, not on your site. For most sites, set **Redirect URL** in the form settings instead. |
| `_token`, `_method` | Stripped automatically so CSRF tokens or HTTP method spoofing fields from frameworks do not leak into submission payloads. |

---

## Minimal Example

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />

  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

---

## Response Codes & Error Handling

When returning JSON, FlowForm responds with predictable status codes:

```json
// 200 OK
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Submission received",
  "id": "22c7a46f-fca5-4ad8-8348-14ccd6fd7cb0"
}
```

| Status | Meaning | Response Body |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `200` | Submission saved (or honeypot triggered) | `{"success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>"}` |
| `403` | Request `Origin` or `Referer` is not in `allowed_domains` | `{"success": false, "error": "Submissions are not permitted from this domain origin."}` |
| `404` | Form does not exist, is inactive, or is not in `endpoint` mode | `{"success": false, "error": "Form endpoint not found or inactive."}` |
| `422` | Validation failure on submitted payload | `{"success": false, "error": "..."}` |
| `429` | Rate limit (`10` requests/min/IP) or owner quota exceeded | `{"success": false, "error": "..."}` (or standard rate-limiter JSON) |

---

## Spam Basics (Honeypot)

Include a hidden `_gotcha` (or `_honeypot`) input in browser forms and JSON payloads. Bots that auto-fill every field trigger the trap and are silently discarded while returning `200 OK`:

```html
<input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />
```

When posting JSON from JavaScript or a framework action, send `_gotcha` along with your form fields:

```json
{
  "name": "Alice",
  "email": "alice@example.com",
  "_gotcha": ""
}
```

---

## CORS & Allowed Domains

FlowForm sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Accept, X-Requested-With` on endpoint responses so browser `fetch()` calls work from any origin without preflight issues.

To lock a form down to your own websites, set **Allowed Domains** (`allowed_domains`) on the form (comma-separated, wildcards supported):

```text
example.com, *.example.com
```

FlowForm checks the request's `Origin` header (falling back to `Referer`). If the domain does not match, FlowForm rejects the submission with `403 Forbidden`. Requests with no `Origin` or `Referer` header (such as `curl` or server-to-server actions) pass the browser origin check.

---

## Choose Your Stack

- [HTML Forms](/guide/endpoints/html) - Zero-JS HTML `<form>` with honeypot and `_next` redirect
- [JavaScript (fetch & FormData)](/guide/endpoints/javascript) - Vanilla browser JS with JSON and `FormData`
- [Next.js](/guide/endpoints/nextjs) - App Router Server Actions and Client Components
- [Astro](/guide/endpoints/astro) - Static `<form>` and Astro Actions
- [Nuxt](/guide/endpoints/nuxt) - Vue `$fetch` component submission
- [SvelteKit](/guide/endpoints/sveltekit) - Server-side form actions with progressive enhancement
- [Static Site Generators](/guide/endpoints/static-site-generators) - Hugo, Eleventy, and Jekyll partials
- [Mobile & Server Clients](/guide/endpoints/mobile-and-servers) - curl, React Native, Flutter, Python, and PHP/Laravel
- [Webflow](/guide/endpoints/webflow) - Native Custom Action and HTML/fetch embeds
- [Framer](/guide/endpoints/framer) - Native Webhook destination and Embed HTML blocks
- [Carrd](/guide/endpoints/carrd) - Custom Send to URL forms and Code Embeds
- [Squarespace & Wix](/guide/endpoints/squarespace-wix) - Code Block and Embed HTML workarounds
- [WordPress](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/) - Classic Custom HTML blocks, headless WP, and page-builder webhooks ([Elementor Pro](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/elementor), [Bricks](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/bricks), [Breakdance](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/breakdance), [Fluent Forms](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/fluent-forms))

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Your `Origin` or `Referer` header does not match the form's `allowed_domains`. Add your domain (including `localhost` during local development) or leave `allowed_domains` blank to allow all origins.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Public endpoints enforce a `10` requests-per-minute-per-IP rate limit (`endpoint-submissions`). Wait 60 seconds before retrying, or avoid rapid automated test bursts from a single IP.
- **CORS preflight errors in browser dev tools:** Ensure you post to `/api/v1/f/{slug}` or `/f/{slug}` and only send standard headers (`Content-Type`, `Accept`, `X-Requested-With`).
- **`_next` redirect ignored (returns JSON instead):** FlowForm only redirects `_next` to the instance's own host or to hosts in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` (`localhost,127.0.0.1` by default). Set **Redirect URL** on the form instead (no server config needed), or, on a self-hosted instance, add your domain to `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`.
- **Redirected to a 404 on the FlowForm domain:** a relative `_next` like `/thank-you` resolves against the FlowForm host. Use **Redirect URL** with your full thank-you page URL.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/html.md -->

# Plain HTML Form

Point any standard HTML `<form>` directly to FlowForm with zero JavaScript. FlowForm stores the submission, sends notifications and, if you set a Redirect URL on the form, sends your visitor to your thank-you page.

---

## Minimal Snippet

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <!-- Honeypot spam trap: keep hidden from human visitors -->
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />


  <div>
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />
  </div>

  <div>
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />
  </div>

  <div>
    <label for="message">Message</label>
    <textarea id="message" name="message" rows="4" required></textarea>
  </div>

  <button type="submit">Send Message</button>
</form>
```

---

## Honeypot Field

The `_gotcha` input sits off-screen (`style="display:none"`) with `tabindex="-1"` and `autocomplete="off"` so keyboard navigation and password managers skip it. If a bot fills it out, FlowForm treats the request as spam, discards the payload, and redirects or responds as if it succeeded.

---

## Success & Error Handling

### Redirects (`_next` vs. Form Settings)

1. **Recommended:** set **Redirect URL** in the form settings to your full thank-you page (for example `https://example.com/thank-you`). FlowForm responds with `302 Found` to it after every successful submission.
2. Per-page override: add `<input type="hidden" name="_next" value="https://example.com/thank-you" />`. FlowForm only follows `_next` when its host is the instance's own host or is listed in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` (self-hosted setting); otherwise it falls back to the Redirect URL. Don't use a relative path: `/thank-you` redirects to that path on the FlowForm host, not on your site.
3. If neither is set, FlowForm returns `200 OK` with JSON:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Submission received",
  "id": "22c7a46f-fca5-4ad8-8348-14ccd6fd7cb0"
}
```

### Handling Errors

In plain HTML submissions, errors (`403`, `404`, `429`) render JSON responses from the FlowForm endpoint. If you want inline error banners without leaving your page, enhance the form with [vanilla JavaScript `fetch`](/guide/endpoints/javascript).

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Browsers send a `Referer` header on native `<form>` submits. If `allowed_domains` is set on the form, include the exact domain serving the HTML page (or `localhost` when testing locally).
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Rapidly submitting a test form more than `10` times per minute from the same IP triggers FlowForm's rate limiter.
- **CORS & Redirects:** Native HTML `<form>` submits are normal browser navigations and are not blocked by CORS. For redirects, use the form's **Redirect URL** setting; `_next` to your own domain only works if that host is in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` on the FlowForm instance.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/javascript.md -->

# Vanilla JavaScript (`fetch` & `FormData`)

Submit forms asynchronously without a page reload using the browser's built-in `fetch()` API. Post to `/api/v1/f/{slug}` to guarantee a JSON response even if the form has a default redirect URL.

---

## Option 1 · JSON Payload (`fetch`)

```html
<form id="contact-form">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />

  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
  <p id="form-status" role="status"></p>
</form>

<script>
  const form = document.getElementById('contact-form');
  const status = document.getElementById('form-status');

  form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    status.textContent = 'Sending...';

    const payload = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form).entries());

    try {
      const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Accept': 'application/json',
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
      });

      const result = await response.json();

      if (!response.ok) {
        status.textContent = result.error || 'Submission failed. Please try again.';
        return;
      }

      form.reset();
      status.textContent = `Thanks! Reference ID: ${result.id}`;
    } catch (error) {
      status.textContent = 'Network error. Please check your connection.';
    }
  });
</script>
```

---

## Option 2 · `FormData` Payload

If you prefer sending `multipart/form-data` directly from a `FormData` instance, omit the `Content-Type` header so the browser attaches the boundary automatically:

```javascript
const form = document.getElementById('contact-form');

form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();

  const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
    body: new FormData(form),
  });

  const result = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(result.error || 'Submission failed');
  }

  console.log('Saved submission:', result.id);
});
```

---

## Honeypot Field

Both examples read `_gotcha` automatically through `new FormData(form)`. Bots that populate hidden inputs send a non-empty `_gotcha` value, causing FlowForm to return `200 OK` without storing spam.

---

## Success & Error Handling

Check `response.ok` before reading `result.id`:

- **`200 OK`:** `{ "success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>" }`.
- **`403` / `404` / `422` / `429`:** `response.ok` is `false`. Display `result.error` to the user, or fall back to a generic message if a `429` rate limit returns `{ "message": "Too Many Attempts." }`.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Browsers automatically send the `Origin` header on `fetch()`. Verify that the page's origin is listed in the form's `allowed_domains`.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Each IP is limited to `10` endpoint submissions per minute. Disable the submit button while the request is in flight to avoid accidental double submits.
- **CORS errors:** Do not set `credentials: 'include'` (FlowForm's endpoint wildcard CORS header is configured for stateless submissions with `supports_credentials: false`), and never manually set `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` when passing a `FormData` body.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/nextjs.md -->

# Next.js (App Router)

Use a Next.js App Router **Server Action** to forward submissions from your server, or a **Client Component** to submit directly from the browser.

---

## Option 1 · Server Action (Recommended)

Posting from a Server Action keeps your FlowForm endpoint URL out of client bundles and works with progressive enhancement:

```tsx
// app/contact/actions.ts
'use server';

export interface FormState {
  status: 'idle' | 'success' | 'error';
  message: string;
}

export async function submitContact(
  _prevState: FormState,
  formData: FormData,
): Promise<FormState> {
  const endpoint = process.env.FLOWFORM_ENDPOINT_URL!;

  const payload = {
    name: String(formData.get('name') ?? ''),
    email: String(formData.get('email') ?? ''),
    message: String(formData.get('message') ?? ''),
    _gotcha: String(formData.get('_gotcha') ?? ''),
  };

  try {
    const response = await fetch(endpoint, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });

    const data = await response.json();

    if (!response.ok) {
      return {
        status: 'error',
        message: data.error || 'Could not submit your message.',
      };
    }

    return {
      status: 'success',
      message: `Received! Reference ID: ${data.id}`,
    };
  } catch {
    return {
      status: 'error',
      message: 'Unable to reach form service. Please try again.',
    };
  }
}
```

```tsx
// app/contact/page.tsx
'use client';

import { useActionState } from 'react';
import { submitContact, type FormState } from './actions';

const initialState: FormState = { status: 'idle', message: '' };

export default function ContactPage() {
  const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(submitContact, initialState);

  return (
    <form action={formAction}>
      <input
        type="text"
        name="_gotcha"
        style={{ display: 'none' }}
        tabIndex={-1}
        autoComplete="off"
      />

      <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Name" required />
      <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Email" required />
      <textarea name="message" placeholder="Message" required />

      <button type="submit" disabled={isPending}>
        {isPending ? 'Sending...' : 'Send'}
      </button>

      {state.message && <p role="status">{state.message}</p>}
    </form>
  );
}
```

Set `FLOWFORM_ENDPOINT_URL=https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us` in `.env.local`.

---

## Option 2 · Client Component

If your Next.js app uses static export (`output: 'export'`), submit directly from a Client Component:

```tsx
// app/contact/ContactForm.tsx
'use client';

import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';

export function ContactForm() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<string>('');
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);

  async function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    setSubmitting(true);
    setStatus('');

    const form = event.currentTarget;
    const payload = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form).entries());

    try {
      const res = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Accept': 'application/json',
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
      });

      const data = await res.json();
      if (!res.ok) {
        setStatus(data.error || 'Submission failed.');
        return;
      }

      form.reset();
      setStatus(`Thanks! Reference ID: ${data.id}`);
    } catch {
      setStatus('Network error. Please try again.');
    } finally {
      setSubmitting(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style={{ display: 'none' }} tabIndex={-1} autoComplete="off" />
      <input type="text" name="name" required />
      <input type="email" name="email" required />
      <textarea name="message" required />
      <button type="submit" disabled={submitting}>
        {submitting ? 'Sending...' : 'Send'}
      </button>
      {status && <p>{status}</p>}
    </form>
  );
}
```

---

## Honeypot Field

Both approaches send `_gotcha`. FlowForm strips `_gotcha` from saved submissions and silently ignores requests where `_gotcha` is non-empty.

---

## Success & Error Handling

- Check `response.ok` (HTTP `200`). Read `data.id` for the created submission UUID.
- On error (`403`, `404`, `422`, `429`), read `data.error` (or fall back to a generic message if the rate limiter returns `429` without `.error`).

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** In Client Component mode, add your Next.js domain (and `localhost` for local dev) to `allowed_domains`. Server Actions do not send a browser `Origin` header by default, so they pass `allowed_domains` automatically.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Server Actions share your Next.js server's outbound IP, so all users submitting through the Server Action share the `10` requests/min/IP limit. For high-traffic sites using Server Actions, prefer direct browser submits in a Client Component so each visitor's IP is rated independently.
- **CORS errors:** Only relevant in Client Components. Ensure you submit to `/api/v1/f/{slug}` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json` without credentials cookies.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/astro.md -->

# Astro

Connect an Astro site to FlowForm with a zero-JS HTML `<form>` on static pages, or use an **Astro Action** when running with SSR.

---

## Option 1 · Static HTML Form

For static Astro sites (`output: 'static'`), render a plain `<form>` inside any `.astro` page:

```astro
---
// src/pages/contact.astro
---
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />

  <label>
    Name
    <input type="text" name="name" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Email
    <input type="email" name="email" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Message
    <textarea name="message" required></textarea>
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

---

## Option 2 · Astro Action (SSR)

If you use Astro Actions (`src/actions/index.ts`) for typed validation before forwarding to FlowForm:

```typescript
// src/actions/index.ts
import { ActionError, defineAction } from 'astro:actions';
import { z } from 'astro:schema';

export const server = {
  contact: defineAction({
    accept: 'form',
    input: z.object({
      name: z.string().min(1),
      email: z.string().email(),
      message: z.string().min(1),
      _gotcha: z.string().optional(),
    }),
    handler: async (input) => {
      const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Accept': 'application/json',
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(input),
      });

      const data = await response.json();

      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new ActionError({
          code: response.status === 429 ? 'TOO_MANY_REQUESTS' : 'BAD_REQUEST',
          message: data.error || 'Submission failed.',
        });
      }

      return { id: data.id };
    },
  }),
};
```

```astro
---
// src/pages/contact.astro
import { actions } from 'astro:actions';
---
<form method="POST" action={actions.contact}>
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />
  <input type="text" name="name" required />
  <input type="email" name="email" required />
  <textarea name="message" required></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

---

## Honeypot Field

The `_gotcha` field is included in both the static HTML `<form>` and the Astro Action `z.object` schema so FlowForm drops automated spam payloads on arrival.

---

## Success & Error Handling

- **Static `<form>`:** Redirects (`302 Found`) to the form's **Redirect URL** if one is set; otherwise returns JSON.
- **Astro Action:** Throws `ActionError` when `!response.ok` and returns `{ id }` on `200 OK`.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Add your Astro site's domain to `allowed_domains` in FlowForm form settings when using client-side `<form>` submits.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Public endpoints enforce `10` requests per minute per IP. With SSR Astro Actions, server-side requests share your server's IP.
- **CORS / Redirect issues:** Set **Redirect URL** on the form to your Astro thank-you page. A relative `_next` such as `/thank-you` redirects to the FlowForm host, not your site; `_next` with a full URL needs your domain in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` on the FlowForm server.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/nuxt.md -->

# Nuxt

Send form submissions from any Nuxt 3 page or component using `$fetch` with reactive loading, success, and error state.

---

## Minimal Snippet

```vue
<!-- components/ContactForm.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const form = reactive({
  name: '',
  email: '',
  message: '',
  _gotcha: '',
});

const pending = ref(false);
const submissionId = ref<string | null>(null);
const errorMessage = ref<string | null>(null);

async function submit() {
  pending.value = true;
  errorMessage.value = null;

  try {
    const response = await $fetch<{ success: boolean; message: string; id: string }>(
      'https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us',
      {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Accept': 'application/json',
        },
        body: { ...form },
      },
    );

    submissionId.value = response.id;
    form.name = '';
    form.email = '';
    form.message = '';
  } catch (err: any) {
    errorMessage.value =
      err?.data?.error || 'Submission failed. Please try again.';
  } finally {
    pending.value = false;
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="submit">
    <!-- Honeypot field -->
    <input
      v-model="form._gotcha"
      type="text"
      name="_gotcha"
      style="display:none"
      tabindex="-1"
      autocomplete="off"
    />

    <div>
      <label for="name">Name</label>
      <input id="name" v-model="form.name" type="text" required />
    </div>

    <div>
      <label for="email">Email</label>
      <input id="email" v-model="form.email" type="email" required />
    </div>

    <div>
      <label for="message">Message</label>
      <textarea id="message" v-model="form.message" required />
    </div>

    <button type="submit" :disabled="pending">
      {{ pending ? 'Sending...' : 'Send Message' }}
    </button>

    <p v-if="submissionId" role="status">
      Thanks! Reference ID: {{ submissionId }}
    </p>
    <p v-if="errorMessage" role="alert">
      {{ errorMessage }}
    </p>
  </form>
</template>
```

---

## Honeypot Field

Binding `_gotcha` to `v-model="form._gotcha"` keeps the input hidden in the DOM while forwarding it in the JSON body. If a bot fills it out, FlowForm silently discards the submission and returns `200 OK`.

---

## Success & Error Handling

`$fetch` automatically parses JSON bodies and throws a `FetchError` on non-2xx responses:

- **Success (`200 OK`):** `response.id` contains the created submission UUID.
- **Error (`403`, `404`, `422`, `429`):** Read `err?.data?.error` inside `catch` and display it in `errorMessage`.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Add your Nuxt domain (plus `localhost` for local testing) to `allowed_domains` on the FlowForm form.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Each client IP is capped at `10` requests per minute. Keep `:disabled="pending"` on the submit button to prevent double submits.
- **CORS errors:** `$fetch` posts JSON directly without cookies by default. Do not add `credentials: 'include'` because FlowForm's public endpoints are stateless.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/sveltekit.md -->

# SvelteKit

Use a SvelteKit **Form Action** (`+page.server.ts`) to forward form data from the server, paired with `use:enhance` on `+page.svelte` for progressive enhancement without full page reloads.

---

## Minimal Snippet

### 1. Server Form Action (`src/routes/contact/+page.server.ts`)

```typescript
import { fail } from '@sveltejs/kit';
import type { Actions } from './$types';

export const actions = {
  default: async ({ request, fetch }) => {
    const formData = await request.formData();

    const payload = {
      name: String(formData.get('name') ?? ''),
      email: String(formData.get('email') ?? ''),
      message: String(formData.get('message') ?? ''),
      _gotcha: String(formData.get('_gotcha') ?? ''),
    };

    const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });

    const result = await response.json();

    if (!response.ok) {
      return fail(response.status, {
        error: result.error || 'Submission failed.',
        name: payload.name,
        email: payload.email,
      });
    }

    return {
      success: true,
      id: result.id,
    };
  },
} satisfies Actions;
```

### 2. Page Component (`src/routes/contact/+page.svelte`)

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { enhance } from '$app/forms';
  import type { ActionData } from './$types';

  export let form: ActionData;
</script>

<form method="POST" use:enhance>
  <!-- Honeypot spam trap -->
  <input
    type="text"
    name="_gotcha"
    style="display:none"
    tabindex="-1"
    autocomplete="off"
  />

  <label>
    Name
    <input type="text" name="name" value={form?.name ?? ''} required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Email
    <input type="email" name="email" value={form?.email ?? ''} required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Message
    <textarea name="message" required></textarea>
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Send Message</button>

  {#if form?.success}
    <p role="status">Thanks! Reference ID: {form.id}</p>
  {:else if form?.error}
    <p role="alert">{form.error}</p>
  {/if}
</form>
```

---

## Honeypot Field

The hidden `_gotcha` input is forwarded in `payload` to FlowForm. FlowForm strips `_gotcha` from saved data and discards any submission where `_gotcha` has a value.

---

## Success & Error Handling

- When FlowForm returns `200 OK`, the action returns `{ success: true, id: result.id }`.
- When FlowForm returns `403`, `404`, `422`, or `429`, `fail(response.status, { error })` preserves the HTTP error code and renders `form.error` without losing the visitor's entered name or email.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** SvelteKit `+page.server.ts` actions run on your Node/edge server without a browser `Origin` header, so they bypass browser origin checks. If you switch to client-side `fetch()` on static routes (`@sveltejs/adapter-static`), add your site's domain to `allowed_domains`.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Server-side actions share your SvelteKit server's IP against the `10` requests/min/IP limit. For high-volume forms, submit directly from `+page.svelte` to `/api/v1/f/{slug}` so each visitor uses their own IP quota.
- **CORS / CSRF errors:** SvelteKit blocks cross-origin browser POSTs to SvelteKit actions unless configured, whereas direct browser calls to FlowForm allow cross-origin `POST` via `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/static-site-generators.md -->

# Static Site Generators (Hugo, Eleventy, Jekyll)

Static site generators compile templates into plain HTML files with no server runtime. Embed a standard HTML `<form>` partial pointing to your FlowForm `/f/{slug}` endpoint.

---

## Hugo

Create a reusable partial at `layouts/partials/contact-form.html`:

```html
<!-- layouts/partials/contact-form.html -->
<form action="{{ .Site.Params.flowformEndpoint }}" method="POST">
  <!-- Honeypot anti-spam trap -->
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />

  <!-- Optional redirect after submit -->

  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

Set the endpoint in `hugo.toml`:

```toml
[params]
  flowformEndpoint = "https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us"
```

---

## Eleventy (11ty)

Create a Nunjucks include at `_includes/contact-form.njk`:

```html
<!-- _includes/contact-form.njk -->
<form action="{{ site.flowformEndpoint }}" method="POST">
  <!-- Honeypot anti-spam trap -->
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />


  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

Define `flowformEndpoint` in `_data/site.json`:

```json
{
  "flowformEndpoint": "https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us"
}
```

---

## Jekyll

Create a Liquid include at `_includes/contact-form.html`:

```html
<!-- _includes/contact-form.html -->
<form action="{{ site.flowform_endpoint }}" method="POST">
  <!-- Honeypot anti-spam trap -->
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />


  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" name="name" required />

  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" name="email" required />

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" name="message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

Define `flowform_endpoint` in `_config.yml`:

```yaml
flowform_endpoint: "https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us"
```

---

## Honeypot Field

Every partial includes `<input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />`. FlowForm detects non-empty `_gotcha` values, drops the submission, and still honors the redirect so bots cannot tell they were blocked.

---

## Success & Error Handling

- **Redirect on success:** Configure **Redirect URL** in the FlowForm form settings with your full thank-you page URL. Don't use a relative `_next` (it resolves against the FlowForm host).
- **No-reload UX:** Add a small progressive script using [vanilla JavaScript `fetch`](/guide/endpoints/javascript) if you want inline confirmation instead of a redirect.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Add your published static site domain (such as `example.com`) to `allowed_domains` in FlowForm. Remember to include `localhost` if previewing with `hugo server`, `eleventy --serve`, or `jekyll serve`.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Public endpoints allow `10` requests per minute per visitor IP.
- **CORS & Redirects:** Plain HTML form posts do not require CORS, but full external URLs in `_next` (such as `https://example.com/thank-you`) require `example.com` to be allowlisted in `FLOWFORM_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS` on your FlowForm instance (or configured in the form's `redirect_url` setting).

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/mobile-and-servers.md -->

# Mobile Apps & Server Clients

Send submissions directly from native mobile apps, CLI scripts, or backend workers using `/api/v1/f/{slug}`. No API authentication token is required for active Endpoint forms.

---

## curl

```bash
curl -X POST https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Alice",
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "message": "Hello from curl!",
    "_gotcha": ""
  }'
```

Success response (`200 OK`):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Submission received",
  "id": "22c7a46f-fca5-4ad8-8348-14ccd6fd7cb0"
}
```

---

## React Native (`fetch`)

```typescript
export async function submitToFlowForm(payload: {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  message: string;
  _gotcha?: string;
}) {
  const response = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      _gotcha: '',
      ...payload,
    }),
  });

  const data = await response.json();

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(data.error || `Request failed with status ${response.status}`);
  }

  return data as { success: boolean; message: string; id: string };
}
```

---

## Flutter (`package:http`)

Add `http` to `pubspec.yaml` (`flutter pub add http`) and post JSON:

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

Future<String> submitToFlowForm({
  required String name,
  required String email,
  required String message,
  String honeypot = '',
}) async {
  final uri = Uri.parse('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us');

  final response = await http.post(
    uri,
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json',
    },
    body: jsonEncode({
      'name': name,
      'email': email,
      'message': message,
      '_gotcha': honeypot,
    }),
  );

  final body = jsonDecode(response.body) as Map<String, dynamic>;

  if (response.statusCode != 200) {
    throw Exception(body['error'] ?? 'Submission failed (${response.statusCode})');
  }

  return body['id'] as String;
}
```

---

## Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us",
    headers={"Accept": "application/json"},
    json={
        "name": "Alice",
        "email": "alice@example.com",
        "message": "Hello from Python!",
        "_gotcha": "",
    },
    timeout=10,
)

data = response.json()
if not response.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(data.get("error", f"HTTP {response.status_code}"))

print("Submission ID:", data["id"])
```

---

## PHP (Laravel `Http::post`)

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

$response = Http::acceptJson()
    ->timeout(10)
    ->post('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', [
        'name' => 'Alice',
        'email' => 'alice@example.com',
        'message' => 'Hello from Laravel!',
        '_gotcha' => '',
    ]);

if ($response->failed()) {
    throw new \RuntimeException(
        $response->json('error') ?? 'Submission failed with status '.$response->status()
    );
}

$submissionId = $response->json('id');
```

---

## Honeypot Field

Include `"_gotcha": ""` (left empty for legitimate submissions) in every mobile or server payload. If populated, FlowForm drops the submission and returns `200 OK`.

---

## Success & Error Handling

Always check the HTTP status code before reading `id`:

- **`200`:** `{"success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>"}`.
- **`403`:** Origin or `Referer` blocked by `allowed_domains`.
- **`404`:** Unknown slug/access key, inactive form, or form is in `wizard` mode instead of `endpoint` mode.
- **`429`:** Rate limit (`10` req/min/IP) or owner quota exhausted.

---

## Troubleshooting

- **403 Forbidden (Origin not allowed):** Native mobile apps and server HTTP clients typically omit `Origin` and `Referer`, which passes `allowed_domains`. If your client manually sets a `Referer` or `Origin` header, ensure that domain is in `allowed_domains`.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Background batch jobs or shared backend proxies sending more than `10` requests per minute from a single IP will be throttled. Space out automated jobs or submit with backoff.
- **CORS:** Native mobile runtimes (React Native, Flutter) and server clients (`curl`, Python, PHP) do not enforce browser CORS policies. If running React Native Web or Flutter Web in a browser, use standard JSON headers without cookies.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/webflow.md -->

# Webflow

Point any native Webflow Form Block directly at a FlowForm endpoint without custom code, or embed an HTML form inside an Embed element.

Reference: [Webflow Help Center: Custom form actions](https://help.webflow.com/hc/en-us/articles/33961334431123-Custom-form-actions).

---

## Option 1 · Native Webflow Form Block (Custom Action)

Webflow's native Form Block lets you override the `Action` URL and HTTP `Method` directly in the Designer:

1. Create an **Endpoint** form in FlowForm (for example with slug `contact-us`) and note its URL: `https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us`.
2. In FlowForm form settings, set **Redirect URL** to your Webflow thank-you page (for example `https://yoursite.com/thank-you`), and optionally add your Webflow domain under **Allowed Domains**.
3. Open your project in the **Webflow Designer** and select your **Form Block** on the canvas.
4. Open **Element Settings** (the gear icon on the right sidebar).
5. Under **Form Settings -> Send to**, remove Webflow's default submission destination if present, click **+**, and add **Custom action**.
6. Set:
   - **Action:** `https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us`
   - **Method:** `POST`
7. Give each Webflow input a clean **Name** attribute (`name`, `email`, `message`).
8. Add a hidden honeypot field (`Embed` element inside the Form Block) so spam bots are filtered silently:

```html
<input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />
```

9. **Publish** your Webflow site and test on the published domain (Webflow Designer preview does not execute external `POST` actions).

---

## Option 2 · Code Embed (Keep User on Page with JSON Fetch)

Because a standard Webflow **Custom action** performs a full-page browser `POST` and redirects away from the page, Webflow's built-in Success/Error state boxes do not trigger automatically. If you want an inline submit state without a reload, use an **Embed** element with JavaScript `fetch` posting to `/api/v1/f/{slug}`:

```html
<form id="webflow-flowform">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />
  <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Name" required />
  <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Email" required />
  <textarea name="message" placeholder="Message" required></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
  <p id="webflow-flowform-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
</form>

<script>
  const form = document.getElementById('webflow-flowform');
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('webflow-flowform-status');

  form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const res = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form).entries())),
    });

    const body = await res.json();
    if (res.ok && body.success) {
      statusEl.textContent = 'Thank you. Your message has been received.';
      form.reset();
    } else {
      statusEl.textContent = body.error || 'Submission failed.';
    }
  });
</script>
```

---

## Plan & Feature Limits to Note

- **Webflow Custom Action Availability & Hosting:** Custom form actions bypass Webflow's native form storage and email notifications (submissions go straight to FlowForm instead of your Webflow dashboard). On Starter/unpaid sites, Webflow caps lifetime form submissions for Webflow-hosted handling and gates **Embed** elements and code export behind paid Site or Workspace plans. Check your Webflow plan tier before adding custom Embed code blocks.
- **Native Webflow reCAPTCHA:** Webflow's built-in reCAPTCHA does not validate forms using a Custom Action. Use FlowForm's `_gotcha` honeypot and Turnstile/hCaptcha verification configured in FlowForm instead.
- **Redirect URLs:** Set **Redirect URL** in FlowForm form settings rather than adding a relative `_next` path like `/thank-you` (a relative path resolves on the FlowForm host). If you pass `_next` explicitly in an Embed form, use a full `https://` URL whose domain is in the form's **Allowed Domains**.
- **Mail Delivery:** Self-hosted FlowForm instances deliver notification emails through the SMTP provider you configure in FlowForm Admin -> Mail Settings.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/framer.md -->

# Framer

Send submissions from a Framer site to FlowForm using Framer's native **Webhook** destination or a custom HTML **Embed** component.

Reference: [Framer Help Center](https://www.framer.com/help/) and [Framer Forms Guide](https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/forms).

---

## Option 1 · Native Framer Form (Send to Webhook)

Framer's built-in **Form** component can post JSON submissions straight to any `https://` URL without writing HTML or JavaScript:

1. Create an **Endpoint** form in FlowForm and copy its JSON endpoint URL: `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us` (note Framer requires `https://` URLs).
2. In Framer, select your **Form** component on the canvas.
3. In the right-hand properties panel under **Send To**, click **Add...** and choose **Webhook**.
4. Paste `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us`.
5. Configure your Framer form inputs with clear field names (`name`, `email`, `message`) and choose either inline **Success/Error** states or a redirect URL directly inside Framer's form settings.
6. FlowForm returns `200 OK` with `{"success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>"}`, which satisfies Framer's `2xx` delivery requirement so Framer does not retry unnecessarily.

> [!TIP]
> Framer's webhook is sent from Framer's servers, not the visitor's browser, so origin checks don't apply to it. To make sure only Framer can post to this form, generate a **server secret** in the FlowForm form settings, append it to the webhook URL (`https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_secret=YOUR_SECRET&_source=framer`), and turn on **Require server secret**. Only do this when the form is used exclusively by the native webhook: a browser embed (Option 2) can't keep a secret.

---

## Option 2 · Custom HTML Form via Framer Embed

When you want full control over `_gotcha` honeypots, file uploads (`multipart/form-data`), or redirect targets:

1. Drag an **Embed** component (`Insert -> Utility -> Embed`) onto your Framer page and switch **Type** to **HTML**.
2. Paste a standard FlowForm HTML `<form>` or JS `fetch` snippet:

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />

  <label>
    Name
    <input type="text" name="name" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Email
    <input type="email" name="email" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Message
    <textarea name="message" required></textarea>
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

---

## Important Notes

- **HTTPS Required:** Framer restricts native **Send To -> Webhook** URLs to `https://` endpoints. Use `POST /api/v1/f/{slug}` for Framer native webhooks so FlowForm always returns JSON (`200 OK`) rather than an HTML `302` redirect (Framer does not follow `3xx` redirects on webhooks).
- **Redirect URLs:** For Option 2 HTML `<form>` embeds, set **Redirect URL** in FlowForm form settings (for example `https://yourframer.site/thanks`), or pass a full URL in `_next` whose domain is listed in **Allowed Domains**. Never use a relative `_next` path like `/thanks`.
- **Allowed Domains:** Add both your custom domain and any `.framer.website` staging domain to FlowForm **Allowed Domains** if you lock submissions down by origin.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/carrd.md -->

# Carrd

Connect a Carrd landing page to FlowForm using Carrd's custom **Send to URL** form action or a raw **Embed** block.

References: [Carrd Custom Forms](https://carrd.co/docs/forms/custom) and [Carrd Embed Elements](https://carrd.co/docs/building/embedding-custom-code).

---

## Option 1 · Carrd Custom Form (`Send to URL`, Pro Plus+)

Carrd Pro Plus plans can point a native Carrd **Form** element directly at an external endpoint:

1. Create an **Endpoint** form in FlowForm and configure its **Redirect URL** in form settings (for example `https://yoursite.carrd.co/#thanks` or your custom domain thank-you page).
2. In Carrd, click **Add Element (+)** -> **Form**.
3. Set **Type** to **Custom**, then choose **Send to URL**.
4. Set:
   - **URL:**
     - Choose `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us` if using **Method: AJAX** (JSON / `FormData`).
     - Choose `https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us` if using **Method: POST**.
   - **Method:** **AJAX** (for Carrd's built-in on-submission message without leaving the page) or **POST**.
5. Under the **Fields** tab, add inputs named `name`, `email`, and `message`.

---

## Option 2 · Embed Code Block (Pro Standard+)

If you prefer pasting a plain HTML form (with a `_gotcha` honeypot field):

1. Click **Add Element (+)** -> **Embed**.
2. Set **Type** to **Code** and **Style** to **Inline**.
3. Paste:

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />

  <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Name" required />
  <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Email" required />
  <textarea name="message" placeholder="Message" required></textarea>

  <button type="submit">Send Message</button>
</form>
```

4. Publish the Carrd site to test (Carrd does not execute custom `<form>` embeds inside the editor canvas).

---

## Plan & Configuration Notes

- **Carrd Plan Limits:** Both native **Custom -> Send to URL** forms (Pro Plus or higher) and **Embed** elements (Pro Standard or higher) require a paid Carrd Pro plan. Free Carrd sites cannot embed custom HTML forms or post to external endpoints.
- **Redirects:** Configure **Redirect URL** in FlowForm form settings or send a full `https://` URL in `_next` listed in the form's **Allowed Domains**. Never use a relative `_next` path like `/thanks`.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/squarespace-wix.md -->

# Squarespace & Wix

Both **Squarespace** and **Wix** restrict their built-in form blocks to internal platform storage and built-in integrations, so neither platform lets you swap the `action` URL of a native form block directly. Instead, add a **Code Block** (Squarespace) or **Embed HTML** element (Wix) containing a FlowForm `<form>` or JS `fetch` snippet.

References:
- [Squarespace Help: Add custom code to a page with code blocks](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206543167-Add-custom-code-to-a-page-with-code-blocks)
- [Wix Support: Embedding a Site or a Widget](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-embedding-a-site-or-a-widget)

---

## Squarespace (Code Block)

1. In Squarespace, edit your page, click **Add Block**, and select **Code** (custom form markup in Code Blocks requires a Squarespace **Business** or **Commerce** plan or higher).
2. Ensure **Display Source** is toggled **off** and set mode to **HTML**.
3. Paste the FlowForm form snippet:

```html
<form id="sqsp-flowform" class="flowform-contact">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />

  <label>
    Name
    <input type="text" name="name" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Email
    <input type="email" name="email" required />
  </label>

  <label>
    Message
    <textarea name="message" required></textarea>
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Send</button>
  <p id="sqsp-flowform-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
</form>

<script>
  (function () {
    const form = document.getElementById('sqsp-flowform');
    const status = document.getElementById('sqsp-flowform-status');

    form.addEventListener('submit', async (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      const res = await fetch('https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Accept': 'application/json',
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form).entries())),
      });

      const body = await res.json();
      if (res.ok && body.success) {
        status.textContent = 'Message sent. Thank you.';
        form.reset();
      } else {
        status.textContent = body.error || 'Unable to submit form.';
      }
    });
  })();
</script>
```

4. Test while logged out (or in an Incognito/Private window), because Squarespace can suppress custom scripts inside the authenticated editor preview.

---

## Wix (Embed HTML Element)

> [!WARNING]
> Wix wraps **Embed HTML** widgets inside a sandboxed `<iframe>`. Avoid relying on FlowForm `302` redirects inside a Wix embed unless your `<form>` explicitly sets `target="_top"` and uses a **Redirect URL** (or full URL in `_next` whose domain is in **Allowed Domains**). In most cases, submitting inline via JavaScript `fetch` to `POST /api/v1/f/{slug}` is much more reliable inside Wix's iframe container.

1. In the Wix Editor, click **Add Elements (+)** -> **Embed Code** -> **Embed HTML**.
2. Choose **Code** and paste the inline JSON `fetch` HTML snippet above (using `https://` for your FlowForm URL because Wix blocks non-HTTPS endpoints).
3. Click **Apply** and resize the HTML element container so the submit button and status message fit without scrollbars.

---

## Limits & Domain Settings

- **Native Form Blocks Cannot Target External URLs Directly:** Neither Squarespace's native Form Block nor Wix's native Wix Forms offers a configurable external HTTP `POST` `action` URL without an automation bridge (such as Zapier, Make, or FlowForm webhooks/REST subscriptions). Use the Code Block / Embed HTML snippets above when you want submissions to go directly from the browser to FlowForm.
- **CORS & Allowed Domains:** If you enable **Allowed Domains** on your FlowForm form, remember to add your published domain. For Wix embeds, note that Wix HTML widgets run in a generated sandboxed origin (leave **Allowed Domains** empty or verify your iframe `Origin` header in browser DevTools).
- **Redirect URLs:** Never use a relative `_next` path like `/thank-you`. Configure **Redirect URL** in FlowForm form settings or use an absolute `https://` URL in `_next` matching **Allowed Domains**.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/wordpress/index.md -->

# WordPress

Connect WordPress sites to FlowForm without installing a WordPress form plugin or configuring `wp_mail` / SMTP inside WordPress.

Reference: [WordPress Custom HTML Block](https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/custom-html/).

---

## WordPress Page-Builder Webhooks

If your site already uses a visual page builder or form plugin with webhook actions, send server-side form submissions straight to FlowForm using an Endpoint Server Secret and `_source=wp-<builder>`:

- [Elementor Pro](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/elementor) - Form widget Actions After Submit (`?_source=wp-elementor&_secret=...`)
- [Bricks](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/bricks) - Form element Webhook action (`X-FlowForm-Secret` header + `?_source=wp-bricks`)
- [Breakdance](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/breakdance) - Pro Form Builder Webhook action (`X-FlowForm-Secret` header + `?_source=wp-breakdance`)
- [Fluent Forms](/guide/endpoints/wordpress/fluent-forms) - Pro WebHooks integration (`X-FlowForm-Secret` header + `?_source=wp-fluent-forms`)

---

## Option 1 · Classic WordPress (Custom HTML Block)

Use WordPress's built-in **Custom HTML** block on any page or post:

1. Create an **Endpoint** form in FlowForm (for example `contact-us`) and set **Redirect URL** in form settings to your WordPress thank-you page (for example `https://example.com/thank-you/`). Optionally add `example.com` to **Allowed Domains**.
2. In the WordPress block editor, click **+**, add a **Custom HTML** block, and paste:

```html
<form action="https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" />

  <p>
    <label for="ff-name">Name</label><br />
    <input id="ff-name" type="text" name="name" required />
  </p>

  <p>
    <label for="ff-email">Email</label><br />
    <input id="ff-email" type="email" name="email" required />
  </p>

  <p>
    <label for="ff-message">Message</label><br />
    <textarea id="ff-message" name="message" rows="5" required></textarea>
  </p>

  <p>
    <button type="submit">Send Message</button>
  </p>
</form>
```

3. Publish or preview the page and submit a test entry. On success, FlowForm redirects visitors to your configured **Redirect URL** (or returns JSON `200 OK` if no redirect is configured or `Accept: application/json` is sent).

> [!TIP]
> **Redirect rule:** Always configure **Redirect URL** in the FlowForm form settings, or pass a full URL in `_next` whose domain is listed in the form's **Allowed Domains**. Never use a relative `_next` path like `/thank-you/`, because relative paths resolve on the FlowForm host rather than your WordPress site.

---

## Option 2 · Headless WordPress (Next.js / Astro)

If you use WordPress only as a headless CMS with a modern front end, wire your front-end routes straight to FlowForm using the framework guides:

- [Next.js Quickstart](/guide/endpoints/nextjs)
- [Astro Quickstart](/guide/endpoints/astro)
- [Nuxt Quickstart](/guide/endpoints/nuxt)
- [SvelteKit Quickstart](/guide/endpoints/sveltekit)

---

## Why Use FlowForm Instead of a WordPress Form Plugin

- **No `wp_mail()` or WordPress SMTP plugins needed for this form:** FlowForm handles form storage, encryption, webhooks, chat notifications, and email notifications (using the SMTP provider configured by the FlowForm instance operator) so your WordPress server never sends outbound contact-form email directly.
- **Zero submission rows in the WordPress database:** Submissions are stored in FlowForm, keeping `wp_posts`, `wp_postmeta`, and custom plugin tables clean across backups, migrations, and caching layers.
- **Clean static caching:** Plain HTML forms work cleanly behind Cloudflare, WP Engine, Nginx FastCGI cache, and static WordPress exports with zero WordPress nonces breaking cached pages.

---

## Current Limits & WordPress Plugin Status

- **No native Gutenberg block or WordPress plugin yet:** FlowForm currently focuses on standard HTML endpoints and REST API/webhook integrations rather than maintaining a separate WordPress plugin.
- **Request a Gutenberg block plugin:** Upvote or share your use case in [Flowformhq/flowform#104 - Request: WordPress block plugin (collecting demand)](https://github.com/Flowformhq/flowform/issues/104).

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/wordpress/elementor.md -->

# Elementor Pro

Route Elementor Pro Form widget submissions to FlowForm via **Actions After Submit -> Webhook**.

> [!NOTE]
> Tested by replaying Elementor's documented webhook format; not yet tested on a live Elementor install.

Reference: [Elementor Help Center](https://elementor.com/help/).

---

## Prerequisites

- **Elementor Pro** (the Form widget and Webhook action are not available in Elementor Free).
- A FlowForm **Endpoint** form (`type: endpoint`), for example slug `contact-us`.
- An Endpoint **Server Secret** generated on that FlowForm form (**Forms -> Edit -> Generate server secret**), with **Require server secret** enabled in form settings.

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

1. Open your page in Elementor and select the **Form** widget.
2. In the left panel under **Content -> Form Fields**, give each field a clean **ID** in its **Advanced** tab (`name`, `email`, `message`).
3. Expand **Actions After Submit**, click inside the **Add Action** input, and select **Webhook**.
4. Expand the new **Webhook** panel:
   - **Webhook URL:** Paste your FlowForm endpoint URL with `_source=wp-elementor` and `_secret` query authentication:

```text
https://forms.example.com/f/contact-us?_source=wp-elementor&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET
```

   - **Advanced Data:** Leave **No / Off** (Simple mode, recommended).
5. Save/Update the page and publish it.

> [!NOTE]
> **Why `_secret` is in the URL for Elementor:** Elementor Pro's built-in Webhook action does not support custom HTTP request headers (`X-FlowForm-Secret`), so query-parameter authentication (`?_secret=...`) is used instead. Keep access logs restricted on intermediate proxies/web servers because URL query parameters can be recorded in HTTP access logs.

### Simple vs. Advanced Data Mode

- **Simple mode (`Advanced Data: Off`, recommended):** Sends flat form fields using your field IDs/labels in `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` format (for example `name=Alice&email=alice@example.com&message=Hello` alongside `form_id` / `form_name`), which FlowForm stores directly as clean top-level submission keys.
- **Advanced Data (`On`):** Wraps submissions in nested metadata blocks (page URL, user agent, IP, serialized field structures), which makes submission payloads much noisier unless you specifically inspect WordPress post context.

---

## Endpoint URL & Authentication Format

```text
POST https://forms.example.com/f/{slug}?_source=wp-elementor&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET
```

- `_source=wp-elementor` tags submissions with `meta.source = "wp-elementor"` in FlowForm.
- A valid secret passes **Require server secret** (`200 OK`, `{"success": true, "message": "Submission received", "id": "<uuid>"}` for JSON callers).
- Missing secret when required returns `403`: `{"success": false, "error": "Endpoint secret is required."}`.
- Invalid secret returns `403`: `{"success": false, "error": "Invalid endpoint secret."}`.

---

## How to Test

1. Open the published WordPress page and submit a test entry in the Elementor form (or replay Elementor's Simple form-encoded request with `curl`):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-elementor&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  --data-urlencode "name=Elementor Tester" \
  --data-urlencode "email=elementor@example.com" \
  --data-urlencode "message=Hello from Elementor Pro"
```

2. Open FlowForm **Admin Panel -> Submissions** and confirm the new submission contains `name`, `email`, and `message`, with `meta.source` set to `wp-elementor`.

---

## What FlowForm Replaces

- FlowForm stores every entry cleanly outside WordPress, dispatches FlowForm webhooks/chat alerts, and sends notification emails using the FlowForm instance's configured SMTP provider in [Mail Settings / Deployment](/guide/deployment) (self-hosters bring their own mail provider).
- You do **not** need `wp_mail()`, WP Mail SMTP, or an Elementor submission database plugin for this form (you can also remove Elementor's **Collect Submissions** / **Email** actions if you want zero local WP storage and zero WP mail).

---

## Spam Protection & Limits

- **Server-side spam filtering:** Elementor submits webhooks from your WordPress server rather than the visitor's browser, so browser-side FlowForm CAPTCHA widgets (`cf-turnstile-response` / `h-captcha-response`) cannot execute during the webhook POST. Keep **reCAPTCHA**, **Cloudflare Turnstile**, or Elementor's **Honeypot** field active inside the Elementor form, and enable **Require server secret** on FlowForm so unauthenticated public callers cannot bypass Elementor.
- **Redirects:** Browser redirects are controlled inside Elementor Pro (**Actions After Submit -> Redirect** using a full destination URL); do not rely on a relative FlowForm `_next` path.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/wordpress/bricks.md -->

# Bricks

Route Bricks Builder Form submissions to FlowForm using Bricks' native **Webhook** form action with the `X-FlowForm-Secret` header.

> [!NOTE]
> Tested by replaying Bricks' documented webhook format; not yet tested on a live Bricks install.

Reference: [Bricks Academy: Form Element](https://academy.bricksbuilder.io/builder/elements/general/form/).

---

## Prerequisites

- A licensed **Bricks** WordPress theme installation (Bricks has no free tier).
- A FlowForm **Endpoint** form (`type: endpoint`), for example slug `contact-us`.
- An Endpoint **Server Secret** generated on that FlowForm form (**Forms -> Edit -> Generate server secret**), with **Require server secret** enabled in form settings.

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

1. Edit your page in Bricks and select your **Form** element.
2. In **Content -> Fields**, confirm each field has a meaningful `ID` / name (`name`, `email`, `message`).
3. Open **Content -> Actions**, add **Webhook**, and open the **Webhook** action settings:
   - **Endpoint URL:** `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-bricks` (or `/f/contact-us?_source=wp-bricks`)
   - **Data Format:** `JSON` (recommended) or `Form data (x-www-form-urlencoded)`.
   - **Headers (JSON):**

```json
{
  "X-FlowForm-Secret": "YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET",
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

   - **Data Payload:** Leave empty to transmit all form fields automatically, or map explicit keys with Bricks dynamic tags (`{{field_id}}`).
4. Do **not** manually add a `Content-Type` header inside **Headers**; Bricks sets `Content-Type` automatically from **Data Format**, and duplicating it can trigger `415 Unsupported Media Type` errors on strict proxies.
5. Save and publish.

> [!TIP]
> Prefer `X-FlowForm-Secret` in Bricks' JSON **Headers** box over `?_secret=` in the URL so the secret stays out of web server access logs.

---

## Endpoint URL & Authentication Format

```text
POST https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/{slug}?_source=wp-bricks
Header: X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET
```

- `_source=wp-bricks` tags submissions with `meta.source = "wp-bricks"` in FlowForm.
- If Bricks custom headers are omitted in an older template, `?_source=wp-bricks&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET` also works, noting query parameters can appear in HTTP server logs.
- Missing or wrong secret when **Require server secret** is enabled returns `403` (`"Endpoint secret is required."` or `"Invalid endpoint secret."`).

---

## How to Test

Replay Bricks' JSON webhook payload directly against FlowForm:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-bricks" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET" \
  -d '{"name":"Bricks Tester","email":"bricks@example.com","message":"Hello from Bricks"}'
```

Verify FlowForm returns `200 OK` with `{"success":true,"message":"Submission received","id":"<uuid>"}` and shows `meta.source = "wp-bricks"` in **Admin Panel -> Submissions**.

---

## What FlowForm Replaces

- Replaces WordPress database entry storage and WordPress outbound mail for this form. FlowForm sends email notifications through the instance's configured SMTP provider in [Mail Settings / Deployment](/guide/deployment) (self-hosters bring their own mail provider).

---

## Spam Protection & Limits

- **Server-side spam filtering:** Bricks fires its Webhook action from your WordPress backend, bypassing browser-side FlowForm CAPTCHA validation. Keep Bricks' built-in honeypot / Turnstile / reCAPTCHA protection enabled on the Bricks form **and** keep **Require server secret** enabled in FlowForm so only your WordPress site can submit.
- **Redirects:** Configure post-submit messages or full-URL redirects directly in Bricks; do not use a relative FlowForm `_next` path.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/wordpress/breakdance.md -->

# Breakdance

Route Breakdance Form Builder submissions to FlowForm using Breakdance's **Webhook** action after submission.

> [!NOTE]
> Tested by replaying Breakdance's documented webhook format; not yet tested on a live Breakdance install.

Reference: [Breakdance Documentation](https://breakdance.com/documentation/).

---

## Prerequisites

- **Breakdance Pro** (Form Builder webhook actions and custom HTTP headers require the Pro license).
- A FlowForm **Endpoint** form (`type: endpoint`), for example slug `contact-us`.
- An Endpoint **Server Secret** generated on that FlowForm form (**Forms -> Edit -> Generate server secret**), with **Require server secret** enabled in form settings.

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

1. Edit your page in Breakdance and select the **Form Builder** element.
2. Under **Content -> Form**, ensure every field has a clean **Field ID / Name** (`name`, `email`, `message`).
3. Open **Content -> Actions -> Actions After Submission** and add **Webhook**.
4. Configure the **Webhook** action:
   - **Webhook URL:** `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-breakdance` (or `/f/contact-us?_source=wp-breakdance`)
   - **Headers:** Add a custom header row:
     - Name: `X-FlowForm-Secret`
     - Value: `YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET`
   - **Field Map:** Map your Breakdance fields (`name`, `email`, `message`) to matching JSON keys.
5. Save the page and publish.

> [!NOTE]
> If your Breakdance plan or setup omits custom headers in the Webhook action UI, use the query parameter fallback instead (`https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-breakdance&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET`), keeping in mind that query-string secrets can be recorded in web server access logs.

---

## Endpoint URL & Authentication Format

```text
POST https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/{slug}?_source=wp-breakdance
Header: X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET
```

- `_source=wp-breakdance` sets `meta.source = "wp-breakdance"` on saved submissions.
- Missing secret when **Require server secret** is enabled returns `403`: `{"success": false, "error": "Endpoint secret is required."}`.
- Invalid secret returns `403`: `{"success": false, "error": "Invalid endpoint secret."}`.

---

## How to Test

Replay Breakdance's mapped JSON POST request with `curl`:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-breakdance" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET" \
  -d '{"name":"Breakdance Tester","email":"breakdance@example.com","message":"Hello from Breakdance"}'
```

Verify FlowForm returns `200 OK` (`{"success":true,"message":"Submission received","id":"<uuid>"}`) and records `meta.source = "wp-breakdance"`.

---

## What FlowForm Replaces

- Replaces WordPress `wp_mail()` / SMTP plugins and Breakdance submission storage for this form. Notification emails are sent by FlowForm via the instance's configured SMTP provider in [Mail Settings / Deployment](/guide/deployment) (self-hosters configure their own mail provider).

---

## Spam Protection & Limits

- **Server-side spam filtering:** Breakdance dispatches webhooks from WordPress PHP after the visitor submits, so FlowForm's frontend CAPTCHA widget cannot validate the browser session. Keep Breakdance's built-in Honeypot / Turnstile / reCAPTCHA enabled on the form, and enable **Require server secret** on the FlowForm form so direct unauthenticated requests are blocked.
- **Redirects:** Configure success messages or full redirect URLs inside Breakdance's Form Builder settings; never pass a relative FlowForm `_next` path.

---

<!-- source: docs/guide/endpoints/wordpress/fluent-forms.md -->

# Fluent Forms

Route Fluent Forms submissions directly to FlowForm using Fluent Forms' built-in **WebHooks** feed with the `X-FlowForm-Secret` request header.

> [!NOTE]
> Tested by replaying Fluent Forms Pro's documented webhook format; not yet tested on a live Fluent Forms Pro install (`WebHooks` feed module requires **Fluent Forms Pro**; free users need a third-party webhook bridge plugin).

Reference: [Fluent Forms Documentation](https://docs.fluentforms.com/).

---

## Prerequisites

- **Fluent Forms Pro** (the native **WebHooks** integration module requires the Pro license; it is not included in the free Fluent Forms plugin without a third-party bridge plugin such as Bit Integrations or WP Webhooks).
- A FlowForm **Endpoint** form (`type: endpoint`), for example slug `contact-us`.
- An Endpoint **Server Secret** generated on that FlowForm form (**Forms -> Edit -> Generate server secret**), with **Require server secret** enabled in form settings.

---

## Step-by-Step Setup

1. In the WordPress admin dashboard, go to **Fluent Forms -> Integrations** (Pro), find **WebHooks**, and toggle it **On**.
2. Open **Fluent Forms -> Forms**, edit your form, and note your field **Name Attributes** (for example `names`, `email`, `message`).
3. Go to **Settings & Integrations -> WebHook** on that form and click **+ Add New**.
4. Configure the feed:
   - **Name:** `FlowForm Contact`
   - **Request URL:** `https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-fluent-forms` (or `/f/contact-us?_source=wp-fluent-forms`)
   - **Request Method:** `POST`
   - **Request Format:** `JSON` (recommended) or `FORM`
   - **Request Header:** Select **With Headers** and add:
     - Header Key: `X-FlowForm-Secret`
     - Header Value: `YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET`
   - **Request Body:** Select **All Fields** or map **Selected Fields** cleanly (`name`, `email`, `message`).
5. Click **Save Feed**.

> [!TIP]
> Fluent Forms Pro supports custom **Request Headers**, so send `X-FlowForm-Secret` as a header rather than `?_secret=` in the URL. If you use a third-party bridge plugin that cannot add custom headers, fall back to `?_source=wp-fluent-forms&_secret=YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET` and keep web server access logs restricted since query strings may be logged.

---

## Endpoint URL & Authentication Format

```text
POST https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/{slug}?_source=wp-fluent-forms
Header: X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET
```

- `_source=wp-fluent-forms` records `meta.source = "wp-fluent-forms"` in FlowForm.
- Without a valid `X-FlowForm-Secret` (or `_secret`) when **Require server secret** is enabled, FlowForm rejects the request with `403`:
  - `{"success": false, "error": "Endpoint secret is required."}` (header/query omitted)
  - `{"success": false, "error": "Invalid endpoint secret."}` (secret mismatch)

---

## How to Test

Submit a test entry in Fluent Forms (or replay Fluent Forms' `JSON` webhook POST with `curl`):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://forms.example.com/api/v1/f/contact-us?_source=wp-fluent-forms" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "X-FlowForm-Secret: YOUR_ENDPOINT_SECRET" \
  -d '{"name":"Fluent Tester","email":"fluent@example.com","message":"Hello from Fluent Forms"}'
```

Verify FlowForm returns `200 OK` (`{"success":true,"message":"Submission received","id":"<uuid>"}`) and records `meta.source = "wp-fluent-forms"`.

---

## What FlowForm Replaces

- Replaces WordPress email notifications (`wp_mail()` / SMTP plugins) for this form. FlowForm sends notifications via the instance's configured SMTP provider in [Mail Settings / Deployment](/guide/deployment) (self-hosters bring their own mail provider) and keeps centralized entries/webhooks inside FlowForm.

---

## Spam Protection & Limits

- **Server-side spam filtering:** Fluent Forms sends webhooks server-to-server after saving/processing on WordPress, bypassing FlowForm's browser-side CAPTCHA check. Keep Fluent Forms' built-in Honeypot / Cloudflare Turnstile / Akismet / reCAPTCHA protection enabled on the WordPress form, **and** enable **Require server secret** on the FlowForm form.
- **Redirects:** Configure confirmations or full redirect URLs inside Fluent Forms (**Settings & Integrations -> Confirmation Settings**); do not use a relative FlowForm `_next` path.
